description: The UCSF Management of the Hospitalized Patient course, chaired by Bob Wachter, MD, is the longest-running and most popular CME course for hospitalists and others who care for hospitalized patients. Taught by UCSF’s top teachers, including Gurpreet Dhaliwal, S. Andrew Josephson, Lekshmi Santhosh, Tracy Minichiello, and Bradley Sharpe, the course highlights recent evidence and current controversies, and blends lectures with multiple interactive workshops to promote active learning. Content areas include critical care, perioperative care, hospital neurology, infectious diseases, cardiology, and nephrology, as well as AI, diagnostic reasoning, and management of the patient with substance use disorder. All of this at the beautiful Hyatt Embarcadero in the heart of San Francisco’s waterfront district. This course is presented by the UCSF Division of Hospital Medicine and is sponsored by the Office of Continuing Medical Education, University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine. It also serves as the West Coast regional meeting of the Society of Hospital Medicine.

description: The Coaching for Health Professions Education certificate is intended for faculty who want to develop skills in coaching health professions learners across schools and across the continuum of education. Coaching has proliferated in health professions education, and many UCSF programs have implemented or are planning coaching initiatives. Coaching learners is distinct from mentoring or advising, and different from career coaching for faculty. This certificate is designed to teach foundational coaching skills and common applications of coaching for educators. Certificate completion requires participation in the day-long in-person session, as well as an activity of participants’ choosing to apply the skills acquired.

description: We are pleased to invite the HPE community to learn about the projects of our 2025–26 Teaching Scholars during this HPE Grand Rounds session. These presentations showcase the Scholars’ learning in curriculum development, assessment, educational theories and frameworks, education research, and leadership. The Scholars featured in this session include: Kamesh Krishnamurthy, MD, PhD, Neurology - Training the Outpatient TBI Neuro-recovery Neurologist: Developing a Consensus-Based Fellowship Framework Shwesha Govil, DO, MPH, Family and Community Medicine - Building a Longitudinal Outpatient Procedures Curriculum for a New Family Medicine Residency Program Arthur Chyan, DO, Anesthesia - Improving Actionable Feedback in Formative Clinical Skills Assessments: Using artificial intelligence tools to provide structured and personalized feedback for oral presentations Learn more about TSP About Health Professions Education Grand Rounds (HPEGR): At these hour-long sessions, participants hear about recent research in health professions education. Presenters may include advanced learners studying in CFE’s master’s and doctoral programs, UCSF faculty who conduct education research, and invited speakers who contribute outside perspectives to advance the scholarly study of health professions education. The Master's Program in Education is a collaboration between UCSF and the University of California, Berkeley School of Education. The program prepares individuals in the research methodologies needed to undertake research studies in health professions education. Students receive mentoring from faculty in the UC Berkeley, Berkeley School of Education and faculty in the UCSF Center for Faculty Educators. UCSF collaborates with University Medical Center Utrecht (UMC Utrecht) to offer the Doctoral Program in Health Professions Education. This collaboration makes possible a rigorous program for scholarly advancement for medical education researchers. Successful candidates graduate with a PhD in Health Professions Education from UMC Utrecht.

description: “The Lymphatic Circulation: Understanding and Treating Pediatric Lymphatic Flow Disorders” Presented by: Gregory Adamson, MD Clinical Associate Professor Pediatric Cardiology Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford Planners expect learners to: 1. Describe the anatomy and physiology of the lymphatic circulation and explain how disrupted flow produces chylothorax, PLE, plastic bronchitis, and chylous ascites. 2. Identify infants and children with suspected lymphatic flow disorders and initiate appropriate workup, including referral for MR lymphangiogram. 3. Identify clinical scenarios where lymphatic disease is misattributed to common diagnoses and examine how diagnostic anchoring may delay recognition and treatment. description: Join UCSF researchers for a practical look at new generative AI models, tools, platforms and workflows designed to facilitate and expedite scientific research! Title: "Benchmarking Automated Scientific Enquiry: When AI co-scientists outpace peer review, what becomes the arbiter of truth?" Featured Speaker: Luca Foschini, PhD President & CEO, Sage Bionetworks Seminar 3-4pm, Networking Reception 4-5pm Share the Flyer! Bio: Luca Foschini, PhD, is President and CEO of Sage Bionetworks, a nonprofit that builds open infrastructure for biomedical data sharing, including the Synapse platform and community challenges such as DREAM. Before Sage he co-founded Evidation Health, where as Chief Data Scientist he spent over a decade leading research on wearable and real-world data for health. He holds a PhD in Computer Science from UC Santa Barbara, has published more than 70 peer-reviewed papers, and in a previous life represented Italy at the International Olympiad in Informatics. Abstract: In under two years, AI systems went from grade-school math to research-level problems, and the length of tasks an agent can complete reliably keeps doubling every few months. More than twenty AI co-scientists now promise to search the literature, generate hypotheses, analyze data and write up results. Do they reason like scientists? Recent evidence says not yet: agents often gather evidence and then ignore it, and better scaffolds barely help. The deeper problem is verification. AI moves fastest where answers can be checked instantly, as in code or proofs, while biology checks its claims at the pace of the wet lab and of peer review. I will walk through what works today, where these tools fail, and how benchmarks run as living community efforts, kept fresh and re-run on every new model, can keep us honest about what is still true., powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform

description: What helps people feel that they truly belong—and what happens when they do? Part of the Fostering Awareness: Dimensions of Belonging series, this session will explore the research behind belonging and the ways our environments, relationships, and everyday interactions can influence whether people feel valued, connected, and able to thrive. Dr. Estrada is Associate Dean of Opportunity & Engagement and Professor in the UCSF School of Nursing.
